| [NOTE-555](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-555.md) | Conceptualization of the Holobiont Paradigm as It Pertains to Corals | A mini-review arguing that corals must be studied as holobionts. The holobiont is defined by location (coral plus microbiota in body, mucus and skeleton), and its membership can change. Traits belong to host–symbiont combinations: a novel anemone–alga pairing out-performed both natural ones in oxygen flux at 32–34 °C, and two octocorals lost symbionts by different routes, one per host cell and one with host cells. It asks, without answering, whether the holobiont is the unit of selection. | Read |
| [NOTE-556](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-556.md) | Defining Coral Bleaching as a Microbial Dysbiosis within the Coral Holobiont | A review that redefines bleaching as three holobiont dysbiosis stages: microbial buffering, Symbiodiniaceae reorganisation by shuffling or switching, and traumatic dysbiosis ending in death (Figure 3). The supporting material is cited and correlational. Vibrio rose from about 0 to 30% relative abundance in bleached corals and returned in resilient ones, but the authors say cause and consequence cannot be separated. "Dysbiosis" names both the disruption and the healthy adaptive response, and the stages have no operational boundaries. | Read |
| [NOTE-558](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-558.md) | Phase Shifts, Herbivory, and the Resilience of Coral Reefs to Climate Change | Four roofless 25 m² cages on Orpheus Island's reef crest kept large and medium fishes out for 30 months after the 1998 bleaching, against four partial cages and four open plots. Macroalgae averaged 56% cover in cages and 4.1% and 1.7% outside. Coral cover reached 7.7% inside against 19.2% and 20.2%. Recruitment fell to about a third (39 against 108 and 118 per 25 m²) and mortality of established colonies was 24.2% against 9.8% and 11.3%. Reopened, the cages lost their algae in 30 days. | Read |
| [NOTE-571](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-571.md) | Catastrophic regime shifts in ecosystems: linking theory to observation | A review of how to tell whether an ecosystem has alternative stable states. Field patterns (jumps, multimodality, dual relationships) are suggestive and never conclusive, since a stepwise driver or a simple threshold produces them too. Experiments can come close to proof: initial-state dependence, lasting shifts after temporary disturbance, and hysteresis. Models show positive feedback must be strong enough. | Read |
| [NOTE-572](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-572.md) | Resilience and Stability of Ecological Systems | Ecological theory had equated stability with behaviour near equilibrium. Holling separates stability (return to equilibrium) from resilience (the capacity to absorb change and persist, set by the domain of attraction), shows they can trade off in lakes, forests, insects and fish, and warns that managing for constant yield can erode resilience. | Read |
